     2	6. Marquise de Cat M
     3	6.1 Overview
     4	The Marquise de Cat occupies the Woodland and wants 
     5	to turn it into an industrial and military powerhouse. 
     6	Each time the Marquise builds one of her buildings—a 
     7	workshop, sawmill, or recruiter—she scores victory 
     8	points. The more of the same building she has on the 
     9	map, the more points she scores. However, to fuel on­
    10	going construction, the Marquise must maintain and 
    11	protect a strong, interconnected economy of wood.
    12	6.2 Faction Rules and Abilities
    13	6.2.1     Crafting. The Marquise crafts during Daylight by 
    14	activating workshops.
    15	6.2.2     The Keep. The Marquise can place pieces in the 
    16	clearing with the keep token, and other players 
    17	cannot. (Pieces may be moved into it. If the keep is 
    18	removed, there is no way to place it on the map again.)
    19	6.2.3     Field Hospitals. Whenever any number of Mar­
    20	quise warriors are removed from a clearing, the 
    21	Marquise may spend a card matching that clear­
    22	ing to place those warriors in the clearing with the 
    23	keep token instead of the Marquise’s supply.
    24	6.3 Faction Setup
    25	6.3.1     Step 1: Gather Warriors and Wood. Form sup­
    26	plies of 25 warriors and 8 wood tokens.
    27	6.3.2     Step 2: Place Keep. Place the keep token in any 
    28	corner clearing. This is your starting clearing.
    29	6.3.3     Step 3: Garrison. Place a warrior in each clearing 
    30	except the clearing in the diagonally opposite cor­
    31	ner from the clearing with the keep token.
    32	6.3.4     Step 4: Place Starting Buildings. Place 1 saw­
    33	mill, 1 workshop, and 1 recruiter. You may place 
    34	them among the clearing with the keep token and 
    35	any adjacent clearings, in any combination. 
    36	5.1 Standard Setup
    37	5.1.1     Step 1: Assign Factions and Starting Player. 
    38	Assign one faction to each player in any way. 
    39	Determine the starting player and seating order 
    40	randomly. Each player takes their chosen faction 
    41	board and the pieces listed on its back.
    42	5.1.2     Step 2: Place Score Markers. Each player places 
    43	their score marker on “0” on the score track. 
    44	5.1.3     Step 3: Draw Starting Hands. If you are play­
    45	ing with two players, remove all four dominance 
    46	cards from the deck. Shuffle the deck. Each player 
    47	draws three cards. 
    48	5.1.4     Step 4: Place Ruins. Place a ruin in each slot on 
    49	the map marked with an “R” (four in total).
    50	5.1.5     Step 5: Form Item Supply. Place these items on 
    51	the corresponding spaces of the item supply near 
    52	the top of the map: 2 M, 2 B, 1 C, 1 H, 2 S, 
    53	2 T, 2 X.
    54	5.1.6     Step 6: Gather Other Pieces. Hand out the 16 
    55	faction overview cards as desired, and place the 
    56	two battle dice near the map.
    57	5.1.7     Step 7: Set Up Factions. In setup order (A, B, C, 
    58	etc.), each player follows their faction’s setup in­
    59	structions, listed in their rules section and on the 
    60	back of their faction board.
    61	5.2 Reach
    62	To set up an interesting game, choose factions whose 
    63	reach values add up to at least the total reach recom­
    64	mended for your player count. (Adventurous players are 
    65	welcome to use any faction mix with 17+ Reach.)

     5	7.2.2     Lords of the Forest. The Eyrie rule a clearing 
     6	when tied for most combined warriors and build­
     7	ings there, and they have at least one Eyrie piece

     9	7.2.3     Disdain for Trade. Whenever the Eyrie craft an 
    10	item, they ignore the listed victory points and in­
    11	stead score only one victory point. (They can still 
    12	score extra crafting points from effects such as Master 
    13	Engravers and the Legendary Forge.)
    14	7.3 Faction Setup
    15	7.3.1     Step 1: Gather Warriors. Form a supply of 
    16	20 warriors.
    17	7.3.2     Step 2: Place Roost and Starting Warriors. 
    18	Place  1 roost and 6 warriors in a corner clearing 
    19	that is not the starting corner clearing of anoth­
    20	er player and, if possible, is diagonally opposite 
    21	from a starting corner clearing. This is your start­
    22	ing clearing. (This is updated from earlier printings 
    23	for flexibility.)
    24	7.3.3     Step 3: Choose Leader. Choose 1 of the 4 Eyrie 
    25	leader cards and place it in your Leader Card slot. 
    26	Gather the remaining leaders face up near you.
    27	7.3.4     Step 4: Tuck Viziers. Tuck your 2 Loyal Vizier 
    28	cards, showing their suit, into the Decree columns 
    29	above your faction board as listed on your leader.
    30	7.3.5     Step 5: Fill Roosts Track. Place your 6 remaining 
    31	roosts on your Roosts track from right to left.
    32	7.4 Birdsong
    33	Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.
    34	7.4.1     Emergency Orders. If you have no cards in your 
    35	hand, draw one card. 
    36	7.4.2     Add to the Decree. You must add one or two cards 
    37	to the Decree, revealing them from your hand and 
    38	tucking them, but only one card added may be a 
    39	bird card. You may add each card to any column, 
    40	and each column can hold any number of cards.
    41	7.4.3     A New Roost. If you have no roosts on the map, 
    42	place a roost and three warriors in a clearing 
    43	with the fewest warriors where all those pieces 
    44	can be placed. 
    45	7.5 Daylight
    46	Your Daylight has two steps in the following order.
    47	7.5.1     Craft. You may activate roosts to craft cards from 
    48	your hand. 
    49	7.5.2     Resolve the Decree. You must resolve the Decree, 
    50	starting with the leftmost column and moving 
    51	right. In each column, you must resolve all of its 
    52	cards, but in any order. For each card, you must 
    53	take the action listed for its column, as follows. If 
    54	you cannot fully take an action, you immediately 
    55	fall into turmoil (7.7).
    56	6.3.5     Step 5: Fill Buildings Tracks. Place your remain­
    57	ing 5 sawmills, 5 workshops, and 5 recruiters on 
    58	the respective Buildings tracks from right to left. 
    59	(Leave the leftmost space of each track empty.)
    60	6.4 Birdsong
    61	Place wood tokens in each clearing with any number of 
    62	sawmills, one wood per sawmill there.
    63	6.5 Daylight
    64	First, you may activate workshops to craft cards from 
    65	your hand. Then, you may take up to three actions—
    66	plus one action per bird card you spend (not as part of 
    67	an action)—in any order and number.
    68	6.5.1     Battle. Initiate a battle.
    69	6.5.2     March. Take up to two moves.
    70	6.5.3     Recruit. Place one warrior at each recruiter. You 
    71	may take this action only once per turn.
    72	6.5.4     Build. Place a building. 
    73	I     Choose Clearing and Building. Choose a 
    74	clearing you rule. Choose whether you want 
    75	to place a sawmill, workshop, or recruiter. You 
    76	will place the leftmost building of its type from 
    77	your faction board. You must be able to pay its 
    78	cost (6.5.4.II) and place it (6.5.4.III).
    79	II     Pay Cost. Find the chosen building’s cost at 
    80	the top of its column. Remove wood tokens 
    81	equal in number to the cost from the chosen 
    82	clearing, any adjacent clearings you rule, or 
    83	any clearings connected to the chosen clearing 
    84	you rule through any number of clearings you 
    85	rule.
    86	III     Place Building and Score. Place the chosen 
    87	building in the chosen clearing, and score the 
    88	victory points listed on the space uncovered on 
    89	your faction board.
    90	6.5.5     Overwork. Spend a card matching the clearing of 
    91	a sawmill to place a wood token there.
    92	6.6 Evening
    93	Draw one card, plus one card per uncovered draw bo­
    94	nus. Then, if you have more than five cards in your 
    95	hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.
    96	7. Eyrie Dynasties E
    97	7.1 Overview
    98	The Eyrie Dynasties wish to restore their once-
    99	dignified kind to their former glory in the Woodland 
   100	by retaking control of the forest clearings. During

     2	8. Woodland Alliance A
     3	8.1 Overview
     4	The Woodland Alliance works to gain the sympathy of 
     5	the various creatures of the Woodland who are dissatis­
     6	fied with their present condition. Each time the Alliance 
     7	places a sympathy token, they may score victory points. 
     8	The more sympathy on the map they have, the more 
     9	victory points they score. Gaining the sympathy of the 
    10	people requires supporters. These supporters can also 
    11	be put toward violent ends, inciting outright rebellion 
    12	across the forest. When a revolt erupts, the Alliance will 
    13	establish a base. Bases allow the Alliance to train offi­
    14	cers, increasing their military flexibility.
    15	8.2 Faction Rules and Abilities
    16	8.2.1     Crafting. The Alliance crafts during Daylight by 
    17	activating sympathy tokens.
    18	8.2.2     Guerrilla War. As defender in battle, the Alliance 
    19	will deal hits equal to the higher roll, and the at­
    20	tacker will deal hits equal to the lower roll.
    21	8.2.3     The Supporters Stack. To take various actions, 
    22	the Alliance spends supporters, which are cards 
    23	on their Supporters stack. Supporters can only be 
    24	spent for their suit and do not count against the 
    25	Alliance’s hand size. Supporters are face down, 
    26	but the Alliance may inspect them at any time. 
    27	I     Capacity. If the Alliance has no bases on the 
    28	map, the Supporters stack can only hold up 
    29	to five cards. If the Alliance would gain a sup­
    30	porter but the stack cannot hold it, that card 
    31	is discarded. If any bases are on the map, the 
    32	Supporters stack can hold unlimited cards.
    33	8.2.4     Removing Bases. Whenever a base is removed, 
    34	the Alliance must discard all supporters matching 
    35	the clearing of the base (including birds) and re­
    36	move half of their officers, rounded up. If the Alli­
    37	ance has no more bases on the map and has more 
    38	than five supporters, they must discard down to 
    39	five supporters. 
    40	8.2.5     Sympathy Tokens. The Alliance has 10 sympa­
    41	thy tokens.
    42	I     Placement Limits. A clearing can hold only 
    43	one sympathy token. 
    44	II     Terms. A sympathetic clearing is one with a 
    45	sympathy token. An unsympathetic clearing 
    46	is one without a sympathy token.
    47	8.2.6     Outrage. Whenever another player removes a 
    48	sympathy token or moves any warriors into a sym­
    49	pathetic clearing, they must add one card match­
    50	ing the affected clearing from their hand to the 
    51	Supporters stack. If they have no matching cards 
    52	(including no birds), they must show their hand to 
    53	the Alliance, and then the Alliance draws a card 
    54	from the deck and adds it to the Supporters stack. 
    55	I     Recruit. Place a warrior in any clearing with a 
    56	roost whose suit matches the card suit.
    57	II     Move. Move from any clearing whose suit 
    58	matches the card suit. (You must move at least 
    59	one warrior.)
    60	III     Battle. Initiate a battle in any clearing whose 
    61	suit matches the card suit.
    62	IV     Build. Place a roost in any clearing you rule 
    63	whose suit matches the card suit and which has 
    64	no roost.
    65	7.6 Evening
    66	Your Evening has two steps in the following order.
    67	7.6.1     Score Points. Score the victory points listed on 
    68	the rightmost empty space of your Roosts track. 
    69	7.6.2     Draw and Discard. Draw one card, plus one card 
    70	per uncovered draw bonus. Then, if you have 
    71	more than five cards in your hand, discard cards 
    72	of your choice until you have five.
    73	7.7 Turmoil
    74	If you cannot fully take an action in the Decree (7.5.2) 
    75	for any reason, you fall into turmoil. You must take the 
    76	Turmoil action as follows in order.
    77	7.7.1     Step 1: Humiliate. Lose one victory point per 
    78	bird card (including Loyal Viziers) on the Decree.
    79	7.7.2     Step 2: Purge. Discard all of the cards on the De­
    80	cree except your Loyal Viziers. 
    81	7.7.3     Step 3: Depose. Flip your current leader face 
    82	down and set it aside, choose a new leader from 
    83	those face up, and place on your faction board. 
    84	Tuck your Loyal Viziers into the Decree spaces 
    85	listed on your new leader.
    86	I     A New Clutch. If you must choose a new lead­
    87	er but none are face up, flip them all face up.
    88	7.7.4     Step 4: Rest. End Daylight and begin Evening. 
    89	7.8 Leaders Reference
    90	The Eyrie have four leader cards, as follows.
    91	7.8.1     Builder. Loyal Viziers begin on Recruit and Move. 
    92	Whenever you craft, you ignore your Disdain for 
    93	Trade special ability (7.2.3). 
    94	7.8.2     Charismatic. Loyal Viziers begin on Recruit and 
    95	Battle. Whenever you take a Recruit action, you 
    96	must place two warriors instead of one.
    97	7.8.3     Commander. Loyal Viziers begin on Move and 
    98	Battle. In battle as attacker, you deal an extra hit.
    99	7.8.4     Despot. Loyal Viziers begin on Move and Build.
